profile.headline: Doing my part for our future robot overlords

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer (iOS)
positions.description:
In my four years working at Walmart, I worked on many projects across three
different applications.

I joined Walmart in 2016 to work on the newly-formed Walmart Grocery app team. As the lead engineer for the Walmart Grocery app, my team and I build an application that was used by more than a million people every month. (The app was retired from the App Store, after its features were merged into the primary Walmart app.)

In mid-2018, I moved to the Digital Acceleration (DA) team. The DA team builds tools for in-store shopping. As the iOS lead engineer, I worked across the DA iOS teams to identify commonalities and make sure great ideas were shared. I also worked directly on our store finder, store details, and online cake ordering platform.

In February 2020, we began working on a ground-up rewrite of the primary Walmart app. I was an influential part of the planning team, co-designing the architecture pattern — a variant of MVVM, using Combine and the “coordinator” pattern. When development commenced I led the engineering team building cart and checkout support. The new app was released late in 2021.

Some key technologies I worked with at Walmart were:
- Foundation, Swift Standard Library, UIKit, CoreGraphics, CoreLocation, and User Notifications for app development
- GraphQL for networking
- Node and Vapor for building mock servers

positions.title: Engineering Lead
positions.description:
Quick Left was a software consultancy specializing in mobile and web software, with a
focus on craftsmanship. (Quick Left is now a part of Cognizant)

As a consultant, I worked on iOS, Node, React, Ember, and Rails projects, using Objective-C, Swift, JavaScript, and Ruby. I led project development teams and worked within established teams.

As an engineering lead, my responsibilities extended beyond developing software. I participated in project scoping and discovery. I helped screen, interview and evaluate potential new hires. And I assisted other team members with code review, mentorship and pairing.

In addition to writing software, I enjoyed being involved with the larger development community. While at QuickLeft, I contributed to open source projects — including, the Swift Package Manager and JSON API specification. I also wrote articles about technology. My work was published in JavaScript Weekly and Docker Weekly.

positions.title: Senior Software Author
positions.description:
Site9 started out as a small web development agency, specializing in WebObjects software. Later, we shifted to building a web application called ProtoShare. It’s used primarily to create interactive prototypes and wireframes. (Site9 and ProtoShare are now part of Astound Commerce.)

Working in a small team of about ten people, with two engineers, we created a rich (client-side) web application, with a server-side application that provides data storage and collaboration. The frontend application was built on a highly-customized version of ExtJS and the backend was built on WebObjects.

As a small company, I had the opportunity to work on all aspects of the application, from frontend to backend; feature design to implementation, deployment, dev-ops, and even customer support.
